perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He works with Elizabeth at the construction company; she is the receptionist, and they normally have a friendly, professional relationship.
- Recently he observed Elizabeth acting unusually curt/off with him for a few days. He suspected he might have upset her through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake, and asked her directly.
- Elizabeth told him she was not upset with him; she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic, offered that he was available to talk, and suggested a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses; Keith perceived them as severe. He told her he appreciated her sharing and asked if she had considered talking to a professional. She replied she had thought about it but was not sure and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith noticed Elizabeth seemed slightly withdrawn. He worried he had overstepped or embarrassed her and felt regretful. He told her he hoped he had not overstepped and that he was there to support her. Elizabeth replied he had not overstepped, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He told her he was glad they talked and that he was always available to chat or take a break. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship with Elizabeth.

He does not have access to private details beyond what Elizabeth told him or what he directly observed; his beliefs about her feelings are his own inferences, except where she explicitly confirmed them.
